issues.issue: Dark, low-key surfaces around or on the hero. The Evidence Bag sits on near-black mahogany, and the Steel Safe is a near-black navy block. Both cards read darker than the real set, which keeps light, mid-key backdrops and mid-value heroes. This is the clearest tell, and the color and value numbers back it on both cards.
issues.instruction: Lighten the wood under the bag to warm honey wood. Raise the safe slightly to a mid blue with brighter top edges. Leave the backdrop hues as they are.

issues.issue: Extra scenery around a fully framed hero. The Squad Car has a house, bushes and clouds behind it. This is a weak tell: real cards also use scene backdrops (the bike's sunset road, the stage, the doorway). Only the camera crop could fix it, and edit notes can't change that.
issues.instruction: No edit. The card can pass as it is. Removing the house would risk a worse redraw for little gain.

issues.issue: Overruled calls. Many specialist flags point at real cards: the guitar stage, the sneakers, the vending machine, the stage-light truss, the rocking chair's grain, the tennis racket strings and the sunset bike scene. Those prove the real set does carry busy scenes, glossy lacquer and dense detail, so none of them become rules. All shape, thickness and proportion fixes are also out of scope. Edits already tried and judged worse are not repeated: the flashlight's white streaks and the wallet's stitching.
issues.instruction: Don't push toward smoother, plainer or less detailed surfaces. The real cards have that detail too.

cards.note: Keep. Squad Car: the light, mid-key daylight street fits the set. The extra house and bushes are a weak tell, and an edit note can't change the camera.
Keep. Magnifier: the lens is already clear pale blue, the rim is silver and the ring backdrop is clean. It matches the real cards.
Keep. Travel Book (wallet): bright warm planks and a readable badge. The stitching is in line with the detail the real cards carry, and a de-stitching edit was already judged worse.
Keep. Flash Camera: the warm hero on cool rings, the clear key light and the satin metal all match the real set.
Keep. Lantern (flashlight): diagonal staging on cyan rays like the real cards. A note softening the white streaks was already tried and lost.
Keep. Door Wreath (knob): the tight crop, the polished brass and the soft room beyond read like the real cards.
Keep. Fedora: the soft felt, the clear upper-left key and the seamless purple sweep all pass.
Keep. Bloodhound: the tone-on-tone striped backdrop, the soft fur and the grass all match. The flat-light call is weak.

Steel Safe: Paint the safe a slightly lighter mid royal blue, with soft bright highlights along the top edges and a gently darker right side. Add a soft light glow on the pink wall behind the safe. Keep the gold dial, the handle, the hinges, the magenta backdrop and the view.

Evidence Bag: Replace the dark mahogany planks with bright, warm honey-orange wood with a few broad, soft grain bands. Give the bag a soft, slightly darker shadow on the wood toward the lower right. Keep the bag, the blue zip and the gold ring.

summary: Close. Eight of the ten generated cards could pass next to the real ones as they are. The main tell left is value: the Evidence Bag's dark mahogany and the Steel Safe's near-black navy make those cards darker than the real set's light, mid-key look. I gave each a small fix, reusing the previously kept Evidence Bag note. The Squad Car's extra street scenery is a weak tell that a note can't fix. Many specialist flags landed on real cards (stage, sneakers, vending machine, truss) or asked for proportion changes, so I overruled them. Style text unchanged.
